lessons.title: Allô! Bonjour!
objectives: Greet people at different times of day
Say goodbye and wish someone a good day, evening or weekend
Choose tu or vous
Say thank you and you're welcome the Québec way

activities.title: Greetings in Québec
activities.instructions: Read through the notes. Tap any French phrase to hear it.
activities.body:
## Saying hello

| French | When | English |
|---|---|---|
| **Bonjour** | Any time until evening, anyone | Hello |
| **Allô** | Friends, coworkers, shop staff, in person or on the phone | Hi |
| **Salut** | Friends | Hi |
| **Bonsoir** | Evening | Good evening |

In France *allô* is only for the phone. In Québec you'll hear it everywhere as a friendly *hi*. In Montréal shops you'll often be greeted with **« Bonjour-Hi! »**. Answer in French and the conversation stays in French.

## Saying goodbye

- **Au revoir**: polite, anyone
- **Salut! / Bye! / Bye-bye!**: friends. *Bye* is very normal in Québec French.
- **À tantôt!**: see you later today (France: *à tout à l'heure*)
- **À la prochaine!**: until next time
- **Bonne journée! / Bonne soirée! / Bonne fin de semaine!**: have a good day / evening / weekend. In Québec it's *fin de semaine*, not *week-end*.

The reply to any of these is **Merci, toi aussi!** or **Merci, vous aussi!**

## Thank you and you're welcome

- **Merci (beaucoup)!**
- Reply: **Bienvenue!** This is the Québec way (literally 'welcome'). **De rien** works everywhere.

## Tu or vous?

Québec uses **tu** more than France does. Use **tu** with friends, family, people your age, coworkers, and usually in casual shops. Use **vous** with older people you don't know, in formal service (bank, doctor, government) and with anyone who uses *vous* with you. If you're not sure, start with *vous*; people will tell you *« Tu peux me tutoyer! »* (you can call me tu).

lessons.title: Je m'appelle…
objectives: Say your name and ask someone's
Use the subject pronouns
Conjugate s'appeler in the present
Spell names using the French alphabet

activities.title: Names, pronouns and the alphabet
activities.instructions: Read the notes and listen to the alphabet.
activities.body:
## Asking a name

- **C'est quoi ton nom?** The most common way in Québec conversation.
- **Comment tu t'appelles?** Casual, everywhere.
- **Comment vous appelez-vous?** Formal.

## Giving your name

- **Je m'appelle Jordan.**
- **Moi, c'est Jordan.** (casual: 'I'm Jordan')
- **Enchanté!** / **Enchantée!** (a woman writes -e; it sounds the same)
- **Pis toi?** = And you? *Pis* is everyday Québec French for *et* / *puis*.

## Subject pronouns

| | singular | plural |
|---|---|---|
| 1st | **je** (I) | **nous** (we), in speech **on** |
| 2nd | **tu** (you, informal) | **vous** (you, plural or formal) |
| 3rd | **il / elle** (he / she) | **ils / elles** (they) |

In spoken Québec French **on** almost always replaces **nous**: *On est de Calgary* = We're from Calgary.

## s'appeler (to be called)

| | |
|---|---|
| je **m'appelle** | nous nous **appelons** |
| tu **t'appelles** | vous vous **appelez** |
| il / elle / on **s'appelle** | ils / elles **s'appellent** |

## L'alphabet

A (a), B (bé), C (cé), D (dé), E (e), F (effe), G (gé), H (ache), I (i), J (ji), K (ka), L (elle), M (emme), N (enne), O (o), P (pé), Q (ku), R (erre), S (esse), T (té), U (u), V (vé), W (double vé), X (ixe), Y (i grec), Z (zède)

Watch out for **G (gé)** and **J (ji)**, which are the reverse of English, and **E** vs **I**.

Accents: **é** (e accent aigu), **è** (e accent grave), **ê** (e accent circonflexe), **ç** (c cédille), **ë** (e tréma).

To ask: **Ça s'écrit comment?** (How is that spelled?)

lessons.title: Je viens de…
objectives: Conjugate être in the present
Say where you're from and where you live
Use à, au and en with cities and provinces
Give your nationality with the right ending

activities.title: Être, places and nationalities
activities.instructions: Read the notes.
activities.body:
## être (to be)

| | |
|---|---|
| je **suis** | nous **sommes** (spoken: on **est**) |
| tu **es** (spoken: **t'es**) | vous **êtes** |
| il / elle / on **est** | ils / elles **sont** |

## Where are you from?

- **T'es d'où?** (casual Québec) / **Tu viens d'où?** / **Vous venez d'où?**
- **Je suis de Calgary.** / **Je viens de Calgary.**

## Where do you live?

- **Je reste à Montréal.** This is the normal Québec way. In France *rester* means 'to stay'.
- **J'habite à Montréal.** Standard, understood everywhere.
- **Tu restes où?** = Where do you live?

## à, au, en with places

- Cities: **à** → *à Toronto, à Halifax, à Gatineau*
- Feminine provinces / countries (most end in -e) and any that start with a vowel: **en** → *en Ontario, en Alberta, en Colombie-Britannique, en Nouvelle-Écosse, en Saskatchewan, en France*
- Masculine provinces / countries: **au** → *au Québec, au Manitoba, au Nouveau-Brunswick, au Canada*
- Islands: *à l'Île-du-Prince-Édouard, à Terre-Neuve*

**à Québec** = in Québec City. **au Québec** = in the province. Locals often say *la ville de Québec* to be clear.

## Nationalities

Add **-e** for a woman (and **-ne** after **-ien**):

- canadien → canadien**ne**
- québécois → québécois**e**
- ontarien → ontarien**ne**, albertain → albertain**e**
- acadien → acadien**ne** (French-speaking Maritimers)
- américain → américain**e**, français → français**e**

Nationalities are not capitalised in French: *Je suis canadien.*

lessons.title: Les nombres
objectives: Count from 0 to 69
Conjugate avoir in the present
Give and ask someone's age
Say and understand a phone number

activities.title: Numbers, avoir and age
activities.instructions: Read the notes and listen to the numbers.
activities.body:
## 0 to 20

0 zéro · 1 un · 2 deux · 3 trois · 4 quatre · 5 cinq · 6 six · 7 sept · 8 huit · 9 neuf · 10 dix

11 onze · 12 douze · 13 treize · 14 quatorze · 15 quinze · 16 seize · 17 dix-sept · 18 dix-huit · 19 dix-neuf · 20 vingt

## 21 to 69

Tens: 20 vingt · 30 trente · 40 quarante · 50 cinquante · 60 soixante

- 21, 31, 41, 51, 61 use **et un**: *vingt et un, trente et un…*
- Everything else uses a hyphen: *vingt-deux, trente-cinq, quarante-huit, soixante-neuf*
- Since the 1990 spelling reform, hyphens everywhere (*vingt-et-un*) are also correct.

Pronunciation: in *vingt* alone the **gt** is silent (*vin*). In *vingt-deux… vingt-neuf* you'll usually hear the t: *vint-deux*.

## avoir (to have)

| | |
|---|---|
| j'**ai** | nous **avons** (spoken: on **a**) |
| tu **as** (spoken: **t'as**) | vous **avez** |
| il / elle / on **a** | ils / elles **ont** |

## Age uses avoir

- **J'ai trente-quatre ans.** (literally 'I have 34 years') Never *je suis 34*.
- **T'as quel âge?** (casual Québec) / **Quel âge as-tu?** / **Quel âge avez-vous?** (formal)

## Phone numbers

- **C'est quoi ton numéro (de téléphone)?**
- **C'est le 514 555-0142.** Numbers take **le**.
- The easy, always-understood way is digit by digit: *cinq-un-quatre, cinq-cinq-cinq, zéro-un-quatre-deux*. You'll also hear groups like *cinq-cent-quatorze*.
- Québec area codes: 514 / 438 (Montréal), 450 / 579 (around Montréal), 418 / 581 (Québec City, east), 819 / 873 (west, north, Estrie), 367, 468.

## Prices

In Québec the **$** comes after the number with a space: **45 $** = *quarante-cinq dollars*.

lessons.title: Comment ça va?
objectives: Ask how someone is, formally and casually
Answer with Québec expressions (pas pire, correct, pas fort)
Recognise spoken contractions: chu, t'es, t'as
Make adjectives agree (fatigué / fatiguée)

activities.title: How are you, Québec style
activities.instructions: Read the notes. This lesson is about how people really talk.
activities.body:
## Asking

| Casual | Formal |
|---|---|
| **Ça va?** / **Comment ça va?** | **Comment allez-vous?** |
| **Ça roule?** (Québec: things good?) | **Vous allez bien?** |
| **Quoi de neuf?** (what's new?) | |
| **Ça fait longtemps!** (long time no see!) | |

## Answering, from great to bad

1. **Très bien! / Ça va bien! / Ça roule!**
2. **Pas pire!** Québec. Literally 'not worse', it means *pretty good*.
3. **Correct.** / **Chu correct(e).** Québec: *okay, fine*.
4. **Bof. / Comme ci, comme ça.** So-so.
5. **Pas fort.** Québec: *not great*.

Always bounce it back: **Pis toi? / Toi? / Et vous?**

## Spoken contractions

In casual Québec speech:

| You hear | It means |
|---|---|
| **chu** | je suis |
| **t'es** | tu es |
| **t'as** | tu as |
| **ouin** | oui (yeah) |

*Chu fatigué* = Je suis fatigué. Use these in speech and texts to friends. Write the full forms in anything formal.

**…, par exemple** at the end of a sentence means *though*: *Chu content, par exemple!* = I'm happy, though!

**T'es-tu correct?** = Are you okay? The extra *tu* turns a statement into a yes/no question. Just recognise it for now.

## Adjective agreement

Add **-e** when talking about a woman: *Il est fatigué. Elle est fatigué**e**.* Adjectives already ending in -e don't change: *Il est malade. Elle est malade.*

Useful adjectives: **fatigué(e)** tired, **content(e)** happy, **occupé(e)** busy, **malade** sick, **stressé(e)** stressed.

lessons.title: Une première conversation
objectives: Hold a full first-meeting conversation
Ask someone to repeat or slow down
Ask what a word means or how to say something
Recognise common fillers (ben, pis, tsé)

activities.title: Survival phrases and fillers
activities.instructions: These phrases keep a conversation going in French even when you're lost.
activities.body:
## When you don't understand

- **Pardon? / Comment?** Sorry?
- **Peux-tu répéter, s'il te plaît?** / **Pouvez-vous répéter, s'il vous plaît?**
- **Plus lentement, s'il vous plaît.** More slowly, please.
- **Je comprends pas.** I don't understand. In speech the *ne* of *ne… pas* is almost always dropped.
- **Ça veut dire quoi, « char »?** What does 'char' mean?
- **Comment on dit « weekend » en français?** How do you say 'weekend' in French?

If someone switches to English, you can say: **J'aimerais pratiquer mon français!** (I'd like to practise my French!). Most Québécois are happy to keep going in French.

## Talking about your French

- **Je parle un peu français.**
- **Je suis en train d'apprendre le français.** I'm learning French.
- **Des fois, je comprends pas.** Sometimes I don't understand.
- **Ça s'en vient!** It's coming along!

## Fillers you'll hear constantly

- **ben** (well…): *Ben, oui!*
- **pis** (and, and then)
- **tsé** (you know)
- **genre** (like)
- **euh** (um)

## Culture: le 5 à 7

A **5 à 7** (*cinq à sept*) is an after-work gathering, roughly happy hour. It's one of the most common places to meet new people in Québec.
